title: See-through or not? Transparent, translucent and opaque

explain.say: Grab a torch and shine it at different things. Sometimes the light zooms straight through, sometimes it gets fuzzy, and sometimes it is blocked completely. Let's sort materials by how much light they let through.

explain.say: See the Transparent group lighting up? Transparent means you can see clearly through it, because almost all the light passes straight through. Window glass, clear water and cling film are transparent. Can you see through your window right now?

groups.label: Translucent
groups.ask: What is the difference between translucent and opaque?

groups.label: Opaque
groups.ask: Why do opaque things make shadows?

explain.say: Now Translucent glows. Translucent things let some light through, but scatter it, so everything behind looks blurry. Tracing paper, frosted bathroom glass and tissue paper are translucent. Why do you think bathrooms use frosted glass?

groups.label: Translucent
groups.ask: What is the difference between translucent and opaque?

groups.label: Opaque
groups.ask: Why do opaque things make shadows?

explain.say: Here is Opaque. Opaque things block all the light, so you cannot see through them at all. Wood, metal, cardboard and books are opaque. Hold a book up to a lamp: can you see any light through it?

groups.label: Translucent
groups.ask: What is the difference between translucent and opaque?

groups.label: Opaque
groups.ask: Why do opaque things make shadows?

explain.say: Opaque things block light, so they make dark, sharp shadows behind them. Translucent things make only faint shadows. Brilliant sorting! Wow fact: press a bright torch against your fingertip in the dark, and it glows red, because a little light passes through your skin and blood.

faq.a: Transparent means light passes straight through, so you can see clearly through it, like glass, clear plastic and clean water.

faq.q: What is the difference between translucent and opaque?
faq.a: A translucent material lets some light through but scatters it, so things look blurry. An opaque material lets no light through at all.

faq.q: Why do opaque things make shadows?
faq.a: Light travels in straight lines. An opaque object blocks the light, leaving a dark area behind it with no light: that is a shadow.

faq.q: Why is frosted glass used in bathrooms?
faq.a: Frosted glass is translucent: it lets light in to brighten the room, but it scatters the light so people outside cannot see in clearly.
Clean, still water is transparent. Muddy water becomes translucent or even opaque, because the tiny bits of mud scatter and block the light.
asks: Why is muddy water hard to see through?

facts: Opaque objects form shadows because light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around them.
A bright light pressed against a fingertip makes it glow red because red light passes through skin and blood more easily than other colours.

quiz.say: You can see blurry shapes through a sheet of tracing paper. What is it?
quiz.why: Translucent materials let some light through but make things look blurry.

wrong.0: Transparent things let you see clearly, not blurry.
wrong.2: Opaque things let no light through at all.

quiz.say: Which material would make the darkest shadow?
quiz.why: Cardboard is opaque and blocks all the light, making a dark shadow.

wrong.0: Cling film is transparent, so most light passes through.
wrong.2: Window glass is transparent and lets light through.
